title: Arlow
text:
Arlow
## Overview

Arlow is a conceptual furniture brand created to explore how restraint, material honesty, and architectural clarity can shape a digital experience. The project focuses on designing a calm, editorial website for a modern furniture studio that values permanence over trend.

The goal was to design a website that feels closer to a quiet gallery than a traditional online store — where objects are given space, materials are respected, and nothing competes for attention. This project focuses purely on the design direction, structure, and visual language of the website.

title: Arlow
text:
Arlow
## The Challenge

Many furniture websites rely heavily on decorative UI elements, loud promotional sections, and aggressive conversion tactics. While effective for mass-market retail, these patterns often clash with the philosophy of boutique design studios. The challenge was to design a website that could:

Present furniture as considered objects rather than products

Maintain a calm, editorial browsing experience

Communicate craftsmanship and material quality without heavy marketing language

Balance minimalism with clarity so users can still explore collections and product details easily

The design needed to feel quiet, confident, and timeless.

title: Arlow
text:
Arlow
## Design Approach

The entire design was built around three principles:

Restraint Every interface element was evaluated and reduced to what was essential. Decorative components and excessive UI patterns were removed in favor of clarity and structure.

Material Presence Furniture is inherently tactile. The design uses large imagery, generous spacing, and matte color tones to allow textures like wood grain, steel finishes, and fabric to remain visible and central to the experience.

Editorial Rhythm Rather than a traditional ecommerce layout, the site follows an editorial rhythm. Sections move between large visual moments, short narrative text, and quiet product grids—allowing the experience to feel slower and more intentional.

title: Arlow
text:
Arlow
## Visual Direction

The visual identity focuses on calm neutrality and architectural structure.

title: Arlow
text:
Arlow
## Color Palette

Soft Black (#1A1A1A)

Bone White (#F5F3EF)

Warm Beige (#D8D2C6)

Stone Gray (#BDB8AF)

These muted tones help create a matte, non-digital feeling—closer to printed editorial layouts than typical web interfaces.

title: Arlow
text:
Arlow
## Typography

Serif: used for headlines and brand expression

Sans-serif: used for body copy and product information

This pairing introduces warmth and character while keeping the interface structured and readable.

title: Arlow
text:
Arlow
## Website Structure

The site was designed around a simple, believable structure similar to what a small furniture studio might use — Home, Shop, Collections, Journal, About, and Contact — with three core collections: Quiet Forms, Soft Structure, and Still Objects. This limited structure keeps the brand feeling focused and realistic rather than overproduced.

title: Arlow
text:
Arlow
## Key Design Elements

title: Arlow
text:
Arlow
## Spacious Product Presentation

Products are presented through large imagery and minimal surrounding UI, so each object feels like a standalone piece rather than a tile in a crowded grid.

title: Arlow
text:
Arlow
## Material Storytelling

A dedicated materials section highlights the brand’s use of oak, steel, and natural linen. Instead of technical specifications, the copy focuses on how materials age, feel, and interact with light.

title: Arlow
text:
Arlow
## Editorial Journal

The journal introduces a slower, narrative element to the site, allowing the brand to talk about materials, design philosophy, and process without disrupting the main shopping experience.

title: Arlow
text:
Arlow
## Quiet Interactions

Micro-interactions were designed to feel subtle and slow. Gentle fades and soft transitions maintain the calm tone of the interface.

title: Arlow
text:
Arlow
## Outcome

The final design presents Arlow as a thoughtful furniture studio rather than a retail platform. By prioritizing restraint, negative space, and material storytelling, the site creates an environment where furniture is experienced as objects with weight and presence.

The project demonstrates how a minimal interface, when carefully structured, can still communicate depth, clarity, and brand identity.

title: Arlow
text:
Arlow
## My Role

Brand concept development

Visual direction

Website UX structure

UI design system

Typography and color strategy

Content and narrative direction

Arlow reads as a thoughtful studio rather than a retail platform, proving a minimal, well-structured interface can still carry depth and brand identity.

Tenuta Palmeri

SCV

## Overview

c.black is the personal brand and consulting practice of Cristina Black, helping premium beauty, fashion, and luxury brands define how they speak, position themselves, and grow.

The goal was to create a series of high-converting landing pages that would integrate seamlessly with the existing website while establishing a stronger conversion path for enterprise-level clients. Beyond designing individual pages, the project evolved into building a scalable landing page system that supports future growth without sacrificing consistency or quality.

title: C.Black
text:
C.Black
## The Challenge

c.black already had an established Squarespace website, but it lacked dedicated, conversion-focused experiences for its growing suite of services.

The challenge wasn't simply to design new landing pages—it was to create a conversion layer in Framer that integrated seamlessly with the existing Squarespace website. Visitors needed to move between both platforms without ever feeling like they were switching websites. This meant:

Designing 6–7 high-converting landing pages that matched the existing brand experience.

Creating a cohesive visual language across both Squarespace and Framer.

Building clear user journeys that guide enterprise prospects toward inquiries.

Maintaining the editorial aesthetic while improving conversion.

Ensuring a responsive, high-performance experience across every device.

title: C.Black
text:
C.Black
## My Role

I led both the design and Framer development of the conversion experience. Responsibilities included:

Designing conversion-focused landing pages.

Developing the pages in Framer.

Creating a reusable component system for future expansion.

Matching typography, spacing, navigation, and interactions to the existing Squarespace experience.

Ensuring users could transition between Squarespace and Framer without any visual or UX disconnect.

Optimizing responsiveness and performance across desktop, tablet, and mobile.

title: C.Black
text:
C.Black
## Solution

Rather than creating a standalone set of landing pages, I designed a unified website system.

Every design decision from typography and spacing to navigation patterns, component styling, and interactions was carefully aligned with the existing Squarespace website so the entire experience felt like one cohesive product.

Behind the scenes, I also built a modular component system in Framer, allowing new service pages to be created quickly while maintaining consistency across the growing site.

title: C.Black
text:
C.Black
## Outcome

The project delivered far more than a collection of landing pages. It established a seamless bridge between Squarespace and Framer, giving visitors the impression of navigating a single, cohesive website while introducing a significantly stronger conversion layer for enterprise clients. The result includes:

9 premium landing pages.

A unified design language across Squarespace and Framer.

Consistent navigation and user experience throughout the site.

A reusable component library for rapid future expansion.

Responsive, high-performance pages optimized for conversion.

A scalable foundation that supports continued growth without compromising the brand experience.

The finished website delivers an entire website ecosystem built around clarity, conversion, and long-term scalability.

title: Sable Records
text:
Sable Records
## Overview

Sable Records (SBL.) is a premium Framer template for independent record labels, artist collectives and music imprints, available on the Framer Marketplace . It is dark and editorial by design: oversized serif type, catalogue numbers and full-bleed photography put the records first and keep the interface out of the way.

The site runs entirely on the CMS. A label adds a release once, and it shows up on the homepage, in the catalogue, on the artist's discography and on its own detail page with tracklist, pressing details and credits.

title: Sable Records
text:
Sable Records
## My Role

This was a self-initiated product. I owned it end to end:

Concept, positioning and art direction for the label niche.

Visual design, type system and colour styles.

CMS architecture across Releases, Artists, Tracks and Gallery.

Framer build, including custom scroll effects and the full-screen menu.

Responsive layouts for desktop, tablet and mobile.

Marketplace listing, preview site and launch content.

title: Sable Records
text:
Sable Records
## The Challenge

Record labels publish in a structured way. A release has a catalogue number, a format, an edition, a pressing and a list of credits. Most templates ignore that and treat a record like a blog post with a cover image.

The goal was to model that structure properly without making the site feel like a database. It had to look like a label with taste, and be simple enough for a small team to update without touching the design.

title: Sable Records
text:
Sable Records
## Design Approach

I took cues from record sleeves and catalogue sheets. Large serif headlines sit on a near-black canvas, while small details like catalogue numbers and pressing info do the quiet work. Photography runs full-bleed so the artwork carries each page.

Motion adds character, not noise. Titles reveal letter by letter on scroll, catalogue text scrambles into place, and release images warp like a spinning record on hover.

title: Sable Records
text:
Sable Records
## CMS Architecture

Releases: catalogue number, format, edition, pressing, price, buy links and credits.

Tracks: linked to releases and split into Side A and Side B.

Artists: bio, discography, booking details and streaming links.

Gallery: categorised images for shows, sessions and artwork.

Format and Gallery category lists to keep filtering consistent.

Releases, tracks and artists are linked by reference, so a single update flows everywhere it appears. That is what makes the template practical for a real label.

title: Sable Records
text:
Sable Records
## Development Process

Researched how labels structure catalogues, releases and credits.

Designed the type system, colour styles and core page layouts.

Built the four CMS collections and their references.

Developed the release, artist and catalogue pages on top of the CMS.

Added the custom scroll effects and full-screen menu overlay.

Tuned every breakpoint for tablet and mobile.

Wrote sample content and launched on the Framer Marketplace.

title: Sable Records
text:
Sable Records
## Results

8 pages: Home, Artists, Artist detail, Releases, Release detail, Gallery, Contact and 404.

4 linked CMS collections, so a release is entered once and shown everywhere.

Release pages with Side A / Side B tracklists, pressing, edition, price and buy links.

Custom effects: letter reveals, text scramble and a warped-record image hover.

Rebrandable through global text and colour styles.

Published as a premium template on the Framer Marketplace.

title: Stella Talverdi
text:
Stella Talverdi
## Overview

Stella Talverdi is a chemical engineer, attorney, and writer with twelve years inside energy infrastructure. She needed a permanent digital home for 74 published essays spanning systems theory, power, desire, grief, law, and cognition. Not a portfolio. Not a blog. A serious intellectual archive built to last.

The brief was unusually precise. Stella knew exactly what the site was, what it wasn't, and what quality of thinking it needed to reflect. That clarity shaped every decision from the first conversation.

title: Stella Talverdi
text:
Stella Talverdi
## The Challenge

The project had three distinct layers of complexity.

The first was design. The aesthetic brief was specific and uncompromising — warm charcoal background, aged parchment tones, oxblood accent, typography as the primary design tool. The site needed to feel inhabited, not decorated. That kind of restraint is harder to execute than visual complexity.

The second was content scale. 74 essays across four categories, each requiring its own CMS page. One template had to serve all of them while preserving typographic quality. Category navigation needed to filter content dynamically from the top navigation links, not just from the sidebar.

The third was technical specificity. The brief called for features that don't exist natively in Framer: an email verification gate with 30-day session memory, bypass URLs for targeted sharing with employers and press, content protection across all essay pages, AI crawler blocking while preserving search engine indexing, and automatic Google Sheets logging of every submission.

title: Stella Talverdi
text:
Stella Talverdi
## What Was Built

6 main pages — Homepage, Essays, About, Work, Thinking in Progress, and Contact. The homepage is a full-screen static image with zero scroll. Four-corner navigation carries the name, tagline, four essay category links, utility links, and a single footer line. Nothing else.

75 essay pages — 74 essays across four categories plus a standalone Rules of Engagement piece, all built on a single CMS template. A toggle in the CMS lets Stella mark any essay as free or gated directly from her dashboard with no developer involvement.

Email gate system — Visitors who click a locked essay see an overlay with a simple email form. On submission, a 30-day cookie is set and the visitor is redirected directly to the essay they came from. Returning visitors with a valid cookie see all essays unlocked immediately with no prompt.

Bypass URL system — Owner-controlled access codes embedded in URLs allow Stella to share specific essays with employers, press, and collaborators without requiring gate completion. Bypass visitors land directly on the essay with a 30-day cookie set silently.

Content protection — Right-click disabled, text selection disabled, and copy keyboard shortcuts blocked across all essay pages and Rules of Engagement.

Google reCAPTCHA v3 — Invisible bot verification on the essay gate form. Runs silently in the background. Real visitors are never interrupted or asked to complete a challenge.

Google Sheets integration — Every email submitted through the gate logs automatically to a spreadsheet in Stella's Google account with a timestamp. No third-party tools, no maintenance required.

robots.txt — 14 known AI training crawlers blocked including GPTBot, CCBot, Anthropic, Perplexity, and Cohere. Google and Bing indexing fully preserved.

Domain connection — stellatalverdi.com transferred from Wix to Framer via DNS update.

title: Stella Talverdi
text:
Stella Talverdi
## Key Decisions

Replaced Framer Auth with a custom gate. Framer Auth's default flow requires full account creation — first name, email, password. That didn't match the brief. It was replaced with a native Framer form plus custom code overrides, giving exact control over the gate experience and eliminating an ongoing monthly fee.

One template for 74 essays. A single CMS template kept the build lean and maintenance simple. The CMS toggle for gating individual essays means Stella can change any essay's access status without developer involvement.

Cookie timing solved a blank page issue. Setting the cookie on mousedown rather than on click or form submit ensures the cookie is written before Framer's redirect fires — preventing the detail page from loading blank.

Preserve URL Parameters was off by default. Framer's native setting to preserve URL parameters across navigation is disabled by default. Enabling it was critical to making the category filter and redirect system work correctly.

title: Stella Talverdi
text:
Stella Talverdi
## Outcome

Full scope delivered within the agreed budget and two-week timeline. Six pages, 75 essay pages, email gate, bypass URLs, content protection, reCAPTCHA, Google Sheets integration, robots.txt, and domain connection — all in.

The site feels exactly as the brief described. Warm, serious, unhurried. The gate protects the work without creating friction for returning readers. The bypass system gives Stella precise control over targeted sharing. Content decisions require no developer involvement.

Where a tool couldn't deliver what was specified, it was replaced with one that could — and the client was told why.

75 essay pages. 14 AI crawlers blocked. One system that works exactly as specified.

Full scope delivered on budget in two weeks: 75 essay pages, a custom email gate, bypass URLs and 14 AI crawlers blocked, all manageable without a developer.

a grounded, editorial typographic scale

warm, textured color tones

structural use of the palm motif (cropped, layered, or partially used for depth)

photography that feels agricultural and place-driven rather than lifestyle-driven

a layout system that balances storytelling + commerce

Working homepage, shop, and hospitality pages
